title: How to get your first short story published online
description: Find a magazine that fits your story, check the submission rules and write a short cover note. Includes a worked example for first-time writers.
intro: Start with one finished story and three places where you would genuinely like to read it. That small shortlist gives you time to read each publication, check its terms and send an editor the version they asked for. Here’s how to go from a finished draft to a first submission.

sections.heading: Find a home for this particular story
paragraphs: Write a one-line description for your own use. For example, “1,800 words of contemporary fiction about two sisters clearing their father’s flat.” That tells you more about where to send it than the description “short story”. A magazine with a 1,000-word flash limit drops off the list immediately.

The Poets & Writers literary magazines directory lets you filter by genre, reading period and reading fee. Shortlist a few possibilities, then open each publication’s own submissions page. Read two recent pieces. If your story and those pieces would make an interesting conversation in the same issue, write down why. That is a better reason to submit than a large following.

sections.heading: Check what the editor is actually asking for
paragraphs: Before you upload anything, look for the word limit, closing date and time zone, fee, eligibility, file type and whether the manuscript must be anonymous. If the listing says submissions are closed, keep the link for later. If the magazine charges a fee and you want a free route, move to the next title on your list.

Check how the publication defines previous publication and whether it allows simultaneous submissions. Mslexia, for example, explains both on its policy page and asks writers to withdraw a piece if another outlet accepts it. Other publications set their own rules. If your story has appeared on a blog or in a newsletter, check the wording before you send it.

sections.heading: Write a cover note that helps the editor
paragraphs: Follow the publication’s instructions first. If it asks for a short note, the title, form and word count are usually a sensible place to begin. Here is an example for a fictional story.
Dear Fiction Editors, please consider “The Spare Key”, a 1,800-word short story, for your fiction section. I write in Liverpool. Thank you for your time and consideration. Best wishes, Alex.

Add a brief biography or a simultaneous-submission statement if requested. A first-time writer can leave out publication credits. Save a clean copy, accept or remove tracked changes and open the exact file you plan to attach. If the editor wants an anonymous submission, check the header and filename as well as the first page.

sections.heading: Keep a record after you send
paragraphs: Make one row in a spreadsheet for the story title, outlet, date sent, version, expected response window and result. Save the acknowledgement with that row. A response window of twelve weeks gives you a date to check the publication’s follow-up policy. An acceptance gives you a list of other editors who may need a withdrawal.

If you write with sound and timing in mind, KiN-TXT also invites independent authors to apply as KiN-Creators. Read the contributor page to decide whether kinetic publication suits this particular piece. The reading buttons on this guide let you experience a pause or a change of pace before you submit your own words.
